title: Data Flow
objective: Generate a row of points from a list and cull it into a repeating pattern of circles.
learn: Lists: one component, many values — and how to filter them.

nodes.need: a list of evenly spaced numbers
nodes.hint: Sets › Sequence. You set a start, a step size and a count.
nodes.correct: Series makes a list: Start S, Step N, Count C. Ten values with step 2 gives 0, 2, 4 … 18. One component, a whole list of data.

wrong.range: Range also makes a list, but by dividing a domain into steps — you set the total span, not the spacing.
wrong.slider: A Number Slider outputs one number. We need a whole list.
wrong.sortList: Sort List reorders an existing list — there is no list yet.
wrong.*: This slot needs a list of evenly spaced numbers.

nodes.need: a component that turns numbers into points
nodes.hint: Vector › Point. X, Y and Z in, a point out.
nodes.correct: Construct Point builds one point per value. Feed it a list and Grasshopper repeats the operation for every item — no loops needed.

wrong.pointParam: A Point parameter only stores points referenced from Rhino.
wrong.unitX: Unit X makes vectors (directions), not points.
wrong.vector2pt: Vector 2Pt needs two points to start with.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that turns numbers into points.

nodes.need: a component that removes items with a repeating True/False pattern
nodes.hint: Sets › Sequence. The Pattern panel already holds True, False.
nodes.correct: Cull Pattern repeats the boolean pattern along the list and keeps only items paired with True. T, F keeps every other point — a rhythm.

wrong.listItem: List Item picks specific indices — it doesn’t apply a repeating pattern.
wrong.reverseList: Reverse List flips the order but keeps every item.
wrong.shiftList: Shift List offsets items by an index; nothing is removed.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that removes items with a repeating True/False pattern.

nodes.need: a component that draws a circle at each remaining point
nodes.correct: Circle runs once per point, so the culled points become a row of circles: a repeating pattern controlled by two sliders.

wrong.polygon: Polygon would work geometrically, but the pattern calls for circles.
wrong.extrude: Extrude needs a profile curve first.
wrong.rectangle: Rectangle would place boxes, not circles.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that draws a circle at each remaining point.

check.prompt: To lay the points out in a row along X, which input gets the Series?
check.hint: Each point should get a different X coordinate.
check.correct: Plugging the list into X gives every point a different X coordinate, so they line up along the X axis. Until then every point sat at 0,0,0.

wrong.Y: Y would also make a row — but along the Y axis. The challenge asks for a row along X.
wrong.Z: Z would stack the points into a vertical column, not a row.
